paragraphs.text: Therefore let us also, seeing we are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
paragraphs.original: Τοιγαροῦν καὶ ἡμεῖς, τοσοῦτον ἔχοντες περικείμενον ἡμῖν νέφος μαρτύρων, ὄγκον ἀποθέμενοι πάντα καὶ τὴν εὐπερίστατον ἁμαρτίαν, διʼ ὑπομονῆς τρέχωμεν τὸν προκείμενον ἡμῖν ἀγῶνα,
paragraphs.translit: Toigaroun kai hēmeis, tosouton echontes perikeimenon hēmin nephos martyrōn, onkon apothemenoi panta kai tēn euperistaton hamartian, diʼ hypomonēs trechōmen ton prokeimenon hēmin agōna,

paragraphs.text: looking unto Jesus the author and perfecter of [our] faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising shame, and hath sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
paragraphs.original: ἀφορῶντες εἰς τὸν τῆς πίστεως ἀρχηγὸν καὶ τελειωτὴν Ἰησοῦν, ὃς ἀντὶ τῆς προκειμένης αὐτῷ χαρᾶς ὑπέμεινεν σταυρὸν αἰσχύνης καταφρονήσας, ἐν δεξιᾷ τε τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ κεκάθικεν.
paragraphs.translit: aphorōntes eis ton tēs pisteōs archēgon kai teleiōtēn Iēsoun, hos anti tēs prokeimenēs autō charas hypemeinen stauron aischynēs kataphronēsas, en dexia te tou thronou tou theou kekathiken.

paragraphs.text: For consider him that hath endured such gainsaying of sinners against himself, that ye wax not weary, fainting in your souls.
paragraphs.original: Ἀναλογίσασθε γὰρ τὸν τοιαύτην ὑπομεμενηκότα ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν εἰς ἑαυτοὺς ἀντιλογίαν, ἵνα μὴ κάμητε ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν ἐκλυόμενοι.
paragraphs.translit: Analogisasthe gar ton toiautēn hypomemenēkota hypo tōn hamartōlōn eis heautous antilogian, hina mē kamēte tais psychais hymōn eklyomenoi.

paragraphs.text: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin:
paragraphs.original: οὔπω μέχρις αἵματος ἀντικατέστητε πρὸς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνταγωνιζόμενοι,
paragraphs.translit: oupō mechris haimatos antikatestēte pros tēn hamartian antagōnizomenoi,

paragraphs.text: and ye have forgotten the exhortation which reasoneth with you as with sons, My son, regard not lightly the chastening of the Lord, Nor faint when thou art reproved of him;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκλέλησθε τῆς παρακλήσεως, ἥτις ὑμῖν ὡς υἱοῖς διαλέγεται, Υἱέ μου, μὴ ὀλιγώρει παιδείας κυρίου, μηδὲ ἐκλύου ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐλεγχόμενος·
paragraphs.translit: kai eklelēsthe tēs paraklēseōs, hētis hymin hōs hyiois dialegetai, Hyie mou, mē oligōrei paideias kyriou, mēde eklyou hypʼ autou elenchomenos·

paragraphs.text: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, And scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
paragraphs.original: ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει, μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται.
paragraphs.translit: hon gar agapa kyrios paideuei, mastigoi de panta hyion hon paradechetai.

paragraphs.text: It is for chastening that ye endure; God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is there whom [his] father chasteneth not?
paragraphs.original: εἰς παιδείαν ὑπομένετε· ὡς υἱοῖς ὑμῖν προσφέρεται ὁ θεός· τίς γὰρ υἱὸς ὃν οὐ παιδεύει πατήρ;
paragraphs.translit: eis paideian hypomenete· hōs hyiois hymin prospheretai ho theos· tis gar hyios hon ou paideuei patēr;

paragraphs.text: But if ye are without chastening, whereof all have been made partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ χωρίς ἐστε παιδείας ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασι πάντες, ἄρα νόθοι καὶ οὐχ υἱοί ἐστε.
paragraphs.translit: ei de chōris este paideias hēs metochoi gegonasi pantes, ara nothoi kai ouch hyioi este.

paragraphs.text: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh to chasten us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
paragraphs.original: εἶτα τοὺς μὲν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν πατέρας εἴχομεν παιδευτὰς καὶ ἐνετρεπόμεθα· οὐ πολὺ μᾶλλον ὑποταγησόμεθα τῷ πατρὶ τῶν πνευμάτων καὶ ζήσομεν;
paragraphs.translit: eita tous men tēs sarkos hēmōn pateras eichomen paideutas kai enetrepometha· ou poly mallon hypotagēsometha tō patri tōn pneumatōn kai zēsomen;

paragraphs.text: For they indeed for a few days chastened [us] as seemed good to them; but he for [our] profit, that [we] may be partakers of his holiness.
paragraphs.original: οἱ μὲν γὰρ πρὸς ὀλίγας ἡμέρας κατὰ τὸ δοκοῦν αὐτοῖς ἐπαίδευον, ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ συμφέρον εἰς τὸ μεταλαβεῖν τῆς ἁγιότητος αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi men gar pros oligas hēmeras kata to dokoun autois epaideuon, ho de epi to sympheron eis to metalabein tēs hagiotētos autou.

paragraphs.text: All chastening seemeth for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yieldeth peaceable fruit unto them that have been exercised thereby, [even the fruit] of righteousness.
paragraphs.original: πᾶσα δὲ παιδεία πρὸς μὲν τὸ παρὸν οὐ δοκεῖ χαρᾶς εἶναι ἀλλὰ λύπης, ὕστερον δὲ καρπὸν εἰρηνικὸν τοῖς διʼ αὐτῆς γεγυμνασμένοις ἀποδίδωσιν δικαιοσύνης.
paragraphs.translit: pasa de paideia pros men to paron ou dokei charas einai alla lypēs, hysteron de karpon eirēnikon tois diʼ autēs gegymnasmenois apodidōsin dikaiosynēs.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore lift up the hands that hang down, and the palsied knees;
paragraphs.original: Διὸ τὰς παρειμένας χεῖρας καὶ τὰ παραλελυμένα γόνατα ἀνορθώσατε,
paragraphs.translit: Dio tas pareimenas cheiras kai ta paralelymena gonata anorthōsate,

paragraphs.text: and make straight paths for your feet, that that which is lame be not turned out of the way, but rather be healed.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τροχιὰς ὀρθὰς ποιεῖτε τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν, ἵνα μὴ τὸ χωλὸν ἐκτραπῇ, ἰαθῇ δὲ μᾶλλον.
paragraphs.translit: kai trochias orthas poieite tois posin hymōn, hina mē to chōlon ektrapē, iathē de mallon.

paragraphs.text: Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man shall see the Lord:
paragraphs.original: Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων, καὶ τὸν ἁγιασμόν, οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν κύριον,
paragraphs.translit: Eirēnēn diōkete meta pantōn, kai ton hagiasmon, hou chōris oudeis opsetai ton kyrion,

paragraphs.text: looking carefully lest [there be] any man that falleth short of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble [you], and thereby the many be defiled;
paragraphs.original: ἐπισκοποῦντες μή τις ὑστερῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ, μή τις ῥίζα πικρίας ἄνω φύουσα ἐνοχλῇ καὶ διʼ αὐτῆς μιανθῶσιν πολλοί,
paragraphs.translit: episkopountes mē tis hysterōn apo tēs charitos tou theou, mē tis rhiza pikrias anō phyousa enochlē kai diʼ autēs mianthōsin polloi,

paragraphs.text: lest [there be] any fornication, or profane person, as Esau, who for one mess of meat sold his own birthright.
paragraphs.original: μή τις πόρνος ἢ βέβηλος ὡς Ἠσαῦ, ὃς ἀντὶ βρώσεως μιᾶς ἀπέδετο τὰ πρωτοτόκια ἑαυτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: mē tis pornos ē bebēlos hōs Ēsau, hos anti brōseōs mias apedeto ta prōtotokia heautou.

paragraphs.text: For ye know that even when he afterward desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no place for a change of mind [in his father,] though he sought is diligently with tears.
paragraphs.original: ἴστε γὰρ ὅτι καὶ μετέπειτα θέλων κληρονομῆσαι τὴν εὐλογίαν ἀπεδοκιμάσθη, μετανοίας γὰρ τόπον οὐχ εὗρεν, καίπερ μετὰ δακρύων ἐκζητήσας αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: iste gar hoti kai metepeita thelōn klēronomēsai tēn eulogian apedokimasthē, metanoias gar topon ouch heuren, kaiper meta dakryōn ekzētēsas autēn.

paragraphs.text: For ye are not come unto [a mount] that might be touched, and that burned with fire, and unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,
paragraphs.original: Οὐ γὰρ προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ καὶ κεκαυμένῳ πυρὶ καὶ γνόφῳ καὶ ζόφῳ καὶ θυέλλῃ
paragraphs.translit: Ou gar proselēlythate psēlaphōmenō kai kekaumenō pyri kai gnophō kai zophō kai thyellē

paragraphs.text: and the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which [voice] they that heard entreated that no word more should be spoken unto them;
paragraphs.original: καὶ σάλπιγγος ἤχῳ καὶ φωνῇ ῥημάτων, ἧς οἱ ἀκούσαντες παρῃτήσαντο μὴ προστεθῆναι αὐτοῖς λόγον·
paragraphs.translit: kai salpingos ēchō kai phōnē rhēmatōn, hēs hoi akousantes parētēsanto mē prostethēnai autois logon·

paragraphs.text: for they could not endure that which was enjoined, If even a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned;
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἔφερον γὰρ τὸ διαστελλόμενον· Κἂν θηρίον θίγῃ τοῦ ὄρους, λιθοβοληθήσεται·
paragraphs.translit: ouk epheron gar to diastellomenon· Kan thērion thigē tou orous, lithobolēthēsetai·

paragraphs.text: and so fearful was the appearance, [that] Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:
paragraphs.original: καί, οὕτω φοβερὸν ἦν τὸ φανταζόμενον, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἔκφοβός εἰμι καὶ ἔντρομος.
paragraphs.translit: kai, houtō phoberon ēn to phantazomenon, Mōysēs eipen· Ekphobos eimi kai entromos.

paragraphs.text: but ye are come unto mount Zion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable hosts of angels,
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ προσεληλύθατε Σιὼν ὄρει καὶ πόλει θεοῦ ζῶντος, Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπουρανίῳ, καὶ μυριάσιν ἀγγέλων, πανηγύρει
paragraphs.translit: alla proselēlythate Siōn orei kai polei theou zōntos, Ierousalēm epouraniō, kai myriasin angelōn, panēgyrei

paragraphs.text: to the general assembly and church of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ κριτῇ θεῷ πάντων, καὶ πνεύμασι δικαίων τετελειωμένων,
paragraphs.translit: kai ekklēsia prōtotokōn apogegrammenōn en ouranois, kai kritē theō pantōn, kai pneumasi dikaiōn teteleiōmenōn,

paragraphs.text: and to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaketh better than [that of] Abel.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διαθήκης νέας μεσίτῃ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ αἵματι ῥαντισμοῦ κρεῖττον λαλοῦντι παρὰ τὸν Ἅβελ.
paragraphs.translit: kai diathēkēs neas mesitē Iēsou, kai haimati rhantismou kreitton lalounti para ton Habel.

paragraphs.text: See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not when they refused him that warned [them] on earth, much more [shall not] we [escape] who turn away from him that [warneth] from heaven:
paragraphs.original: Βλέπετε μὴ παραιτήσησθε τὸν λαλοῦντα· εἰ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι οὐκ ἐξέφυγον ἐπὶ γῆς παραιτησάμενοι τὸν χρηματίζοντα, πολὺ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς οἱ τὸν ἀπʼ οὐρανῶν ἀποστρεφόμενοι·
paragraphs.translit: Blepete mē paraitēsēsthe ton lalounta· ei gar ekeinoi ouk exephygon epi gēs paraitēsamenoi ton chrēmatizonta, poly mallon hēmeis hoi ton apʼ ouranōn apostrephomenoi·

paragraphs.text: whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more will I make to tremble not the earth only, but also the heaven.
paragraphs.original: οὗ ἡ φωνὴ τὴν γῆν ἐσάλευσεν τότε, νῦν δὲ ἐπήγγελται λέγων· Ἔτι ἅπαξ ἐγὼ σείσω οὐ μόνον τὴν γῆν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν οὐρανόν.
paragraphs.translit: hou hē phōnē tēn gēn esaleusen tote, nyn de epēngeltai legōn· Eti hapax egō seisō ou monon tēn gēn alla kai ton ouranon.

paragraphs.text: And this [word], Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that have been made, that those things which are not shaken may remain.
paragraphs.original: τὸ δὲ Ἔτι ἅπαξ δηλοῖ τῶν σαλευομένων μετάθεσιν ὡς πεποιημένων, ἵνα μείνῃ τὰ μὴ σαλευόμενα.
paragraphs.translit: to de Eti hapax dēloi tōn saleuomenōn metathesin hōs pepoiēmenōn, hina meinē ta mē saleuomena.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us have grace, whereby we may offer service well-pleasing to God with reverence and awe:
paragraphs.original: διὸ βασιλείαν ἀσάλευτον παραλαμβάνοντες ἔχωμεν χάριν, διʼ ἧς λατρεύωμεν εὐαρέστως τῷ θεῷ μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ δέους,
paragraphs.translit: dio basileian asaleuton paralambanontes echōmen charin, diʼ hēs latreuōmen euarestōs tō theō meta eulabeias kai deous,

paragraphs.text: for our God is a consuming fire.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν πῦρ καταναλίσκον.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar ho theos hēmōn pyr katanaliskon.
